title: Terraform support for Dedicated scaling policy (min/max bounds + predictive mode)
creator: Irene Choi
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
Enterprise Dedicated customers are requesting Infrastructure-as-Code support to configure autoscaling bounds and predictive mode, so scaling behavior is auditable and consistent across environments (see Lumen Legaltech + Northstar Fintech asks; tracked via CS/Sales).

This ticket adds support in the redwood-terraform provider/modules for:
- autoscaling bounds: min/max replicas (and any required cooldown/guardrail fields exposed by the control plane)
- predictive autoscaling toggle/mode: enable/disable + any basic knobs that are stable and GA-ready

Why now
- Pilot/GA readiness requires customers can manage scaling policy via API/Console AND IaC.
- Several enterprise procurement/security reviews explicitly require IaC + change management workflow (Terraform plan/apply + logs).

Scope
1) Provider schema updates
- Add a nested block or top-level attributes (TBD by provider conventions) under the Dedicated deployment resource to manage scaling policy.
- Map Terraform config fields to the control plane API fields introduced in ENG-22141/ENG-22153.

2) Validation + UX
- Validate min_replicas >= 0 (or >= 1 if we disallow 0), max_replicas >= min_replicas.
- If predictive mode is set, surface a helpful error if feature flag isn’t enabled (expect API to enforce; provider should provide a clear message when it fails).
- Ensure diffs are stable (defaults should not cause perpetual drift).

3) Read/Import/Drift behavior
- Read-after-write: provider should re-read the scaling policy after update and store computed fields.
- Import should populate scaling policy fields when importing an existing deployment.
- Avoid “unknown -> default -> diff” loops; computed vs optional+default must be chosen carefully.

4) Examples + docs
- Add at least one example config for:
  a) bounds only
  b) bounds + predictive enabled (noting feature flag requirement)
- Update module README and provider docs to describe semantics and any non-obvious behaviors.

Non-goals
- Implementing forecasting itself (handled by platform)
- Supporting every internal-only tuning knob (keep to stable, customer-facing API fields)
- Contract enforcement workflows (handled outside product)

Proposed Terraform interface (initial)
Resource: redwood_dedicated_deployment (or module wrapper)

Option A (nested block; preferred for clarity):
scaling_policy {
  enabled          = true
  min_replicas     = 4
  max_replicas     = 24
  cooldown_seconds = 300

  predictive {
    enabled = true
    mode    = "BIAS_REACTIVE"  # or "PREDICTIVE_WITH_REACTIVE_FALLBACK" (match API enum)
  }
}

Option B (flattened fields) if provider style discourages nested blocks.

Implementation plan
- Align on exact field names/enums with control plane schema (ENG-22141 / schema PRs) before finalizing.
- Update provider:
  - add schema fields
  - implement Create/Read/Update mapping
  - add acceptance tests (mock API) for:
    - bounds set + read back
    - min>max validation
    - predictive enabled (API rejects when flag off → provider surfaces error)
    - import populates scaling policy
- Update modules:
  - expose variables for min/max/predictive
  - update examples

Acceptance criteria
- Customers can configure min/max bounds via Terraform and observe it reflected in Console/API.
- Customers can enable predictive mode via Terraform where feature flag is enabled.
- No perpetual diffs when only defaults are present (plan/apply is idempotent).
- Import works for existing Dedicated deployments and includes scaling policy state.
- Docs/examples merged and linked from release notes / CS enablement.

Testing
- Unit tests for schema validation.
- Provider acceptance/integration tests using a recorded/stubbed control plane API response.
- Manual smoke test in staging:
  1) create deployment with bounds
  2) update bounds
  3) toggle predictive on/off
  4) terraform import existing deployment and verify plan is empty

Risks / gotchas
- API defaults/backfills: if server omits fields when unset, provider must treat them as Computed (or set defaults explicitly) to avoid drift.
- Enum churn during pilot: predictive mode enums may change; coordinate with Platform Control Plane (Ethan/Jordan) before shipping.
- Feature flags: predictive mode requires account/deployment flag; failure messages should instruct how to request enablement.

Progress updates
- 2025-08-13 (Diego): Synced with Ethan Park on field names + enum stability; targeting minimal stable fields: min_replicas, max_replicas, cooldown_seconds, predictive_enabled + predictive_mode.
- 2025-08-18 (Diego): Implemented provider schema + update mapping; running into drift due to server default cooldown_seconds omitted when unset. Plan: mark cooldown_seconds as Optional+Computed and only send when set.
- 2025-08-22 (Diego): Added import read for scaling policy; verified bounds-only config is idempotent in staging.
- 2025-08-26 (Diego): Predictive toggle tested with pilot account flag on; without flag API returns 403 w/ reason=FEATURE_DISABLED—provider now surfaces actionable error.
- 2025-09-05 (Connor O'Brien): Marking Done after provider + module changes merged and docs/examples included; coordinate comms via CS playbook.

- Code: sources/github/redwood-terraform/pr-612-expose-scaling-policy-min-max-in-dedicated-modules.json
- Customer docs follow-up: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2442-dedicated-autoscaling-bounds-customer-docs.json (ensure Terraform example is referenced)

Notes for CS/TAM
- Predictive mode via Terraform will fail unless the account/deployment feature flag is enabled. Point customers to internal enablement flow (INT-9412) or follow standard pilot enrollment process.
- If customer sets a high min bound, region capacity shortages may prevent fulfillment; expected behavior and comms covered in ENG-22151 + runbooks.
